claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-type high-entropy alloy will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with conventional alloys under elevated-temperature mechanical-wear conditions.
The multi-element composition of AlCoCrFeNi promotes rapid formation of a stable, protective oxide layer.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The proposed exposure combines cyclic mechanical wear, a corrosive medium, and elevated temperature.
Representative test conditions are approximately 500°C in a chloride-containing medium with repeated mechanical wear.
A stable, adherent oxide layer forms on the alloy surface during exposure.
Under combined thermal and mechanical stress, the alloy composition facilitates rapid surface oxidation.
Rapid surface oxidation produces a passivating oxide film.
The passivating oxide film minimizes further corrosion and mechanical degradation.
AlCoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than a conventional alloy under identical test conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will have a lower corrosion rate than a conventional alloy under identical test conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will form a thicker and more uniform oxide scale than a conventional alloy under identical test conditions.
Conventional structural alloys used in extreme environments form protective oxide films less effectively than AlCoCrFeNi.
Protective behavior may be compromised above the oxide film's temperature-stability limit.
Prolonged wear that disrupts film formation may compromise the alloy's protective behavior.
A greater than 20% statistically significant improvement in wear and corrosion rates is proposed as the performance criterion.
Failure to form a continuous protective oxide layer relative to the conventional-alloy control would falsify the hypothesis.
